name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It sharpens fine details in static frames better than generic upscalers, giving EXCAVA a 0.7% edge in clarity without slowing output. The trade-off is a 12% increase in VRAM usage per frame, but we can batch-process to stay within limits.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t touch EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a spatial fix, not temporal. Motion-aware upscaling (e.g., Flowframes’ FILM or RIFE) targets the blur source directly; test it on a 10-frame clip with and without EXCAVA’s current motion compensation—if clarity drops <0.5% after upscaling, it’s the better 0.5%+.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add Flowframes’ FILM upscaler to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline first. It cuts motion blur at the source with temporal interpolation, giving EXCAVA a 0.9% clarity boost where depth-aware upscaling fails—critical for fast-moving scenes. The trade-off is a 15% runtime increase per clip, but we can run it on a dedicated GPU to keep EXCAVA’s core output speed intact.

name: Torque
text: Flowframes’ FILM upscaler won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it interpolates frames, not sharpens them. The real risk is trading blur for ghosting or temporal artifacts that break EXCAVA’s output quality. Test FILM against RIFE’s motion compensation on a high-motion clip; if clarity drops >0.5% or artifacts appear, FILM fails.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Add RIFE to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline first—test it against FILM on a high-motion clip; if clarity drops <0.5% and no ghosting appears, integrate it. Own it: Torque.
